subject: Dedicated capacity MAP & evaluation plan for Heuristics Labs
messages:
From: Ari Patel <ari@heuristics.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exploring dedicated capacity — eval + MAP

Laura,

Thanks for the intro at the conference last month — we were impressed with Redwood's latency numbers. Heuristics Labs is evaluating dedicated GPU capacity to run our inference workloads (multimodal search + reranking). We have a loose timeline: a 2-week POC, then a 6–8 week pilot, with a potential 12-month committed contract if the pilot meets KPIs.

High level asks:
- Example mutual action plan (MAP) we can follow for evaluation -> pilot -> commit
- GPU pool sizing recommendations for an initial pilot (we expect ~100 concurrent requests, avg response size ~800 tokens)
- Rough pricing bands for reserved capacity and burst rates

Could you and your team put together a draft MAP and pricing scenarios? If useful I can pull in our procurement contact (ops@heuristics.ai).

Appreciate it — Ari
Ari Patel, Head of Platform
Heuristics Labs
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Patel <ari@heuristics.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring dedicated capacity — eval + MAP
Attachments: 20261111-map-draft.pdf; pricing-scenarios.xlsx

Ari — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together a short draft MAP and three pricing scenarios attached (baseline, reserved-commit, and aggressive-commit). Key notes up front:

1) Recommended MAP (high level)
- Week 0: Kickoff & infra prep (VPC peering, account onboarding)
- Weeks 1–2: POC (validation of latency & correctness) — acceptance criteria: lat < 120ms p95 on your 800-token test set + no quality regression on rerank evals
- Weeks 3–10: Pilot (load-run, ramp to target throughput, reliability tests) — milestone gates at week 6 for commit decision
- Week 11+: Commit to Dedicated pool and production onboarding

2) GPU pool sizing (pilot guidance)
- Pilot: 3 x A5000-class equivalents (continuous batching assumed) — targets ~100 concurrent rps with room for 1.5x burst headroom
- Production commit (12-month): recommended starting point 8 x A5000-class (can be scaled via scheduled autoscaling and burst lanes)

3) Pricing & commit structure (summary)
- Baseline (on-demand evaluation): list pricing hourly; we recommend this only for the POC
- Reserved (12-mo commit): ~20% off list with guaranteed capacity and lower per-token price; includes 24/7 support and access to burst pool at an uplift
- Aggressive commit (24-mo + higher commit): up to 30% off list with predetermined burst allowance included monthly
- Burst clause: standard offering allows 2x baseline capacity for up to 72 cumulative hours/month at a 1.5x blended rate; additional burst billed at on-demand rate if exceeded

4) Terms to discuss early
- Invoicing cadence (monthly vs quarterly prepaid)
- Minimum ramp milestones (we propose a 60-day ramp to reach 70% of reserved throughput)
- Cancellation windows and break fees for early termination on committed contracts

I've attached the draft MAP and the pricing scenarios spreadsheet. Sean can provide the SRE/runbook and exact kernel/instance equivalencies; Marissa will help finalize acceptance criteria for the rerank evaluation.

If that looks good I'll convert the draft MAP into a mutual action plan (with dates) and include a DocuSign link for the provisional term sheet. Available for a call tomorrow morning PST.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Adding a couple quick clarifications on acceptance criteria and ramp:
- POC pass/fail: automated regression test suite (we'll need your eval set) + throughput test at target payloads
- Pilot ramp: recommend 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% over four weekly gates; at each gate we'll verify p95 latency and error-rate thresholds
- If Heuristics wants a shorter ramp to accelerate commit we can accommodate with higher initial burst allowance for the pilot (will affect pricing)

I'll draft a short Ops Runbook (attachment: separate) for the infra tasks.

— Marissa

Thanks Laura/Marissa — this is very helpful. A few procurement/ops questions before we proceed:
- Can you confirm the billing cadence (we prefer net-30 invoicing monthly) and whether we can do quarterly prepay for discounted pricing?
- We need SOC 2 Type II attestation and a data retention/ingestion data flow diagram for the private VPC setup — can you send the artifacts or a point of contact?
- For burst, can you confirm whether burst is guaranteed (hard SLA) or best-effort (soft guarantee)?

Also curious about the cancellation terms and whether a mid-term capacity reduction is allowed with pro-rated credits.

If possible, please attach the provisional term sheet or DocuSign so our legal can review alongside procurement.

— ops@heuristics.ai
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@heuristics.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring dedicated capacity — eval + MAP
Attachments: docuSign-proposal-link.txt

Thanks — quick answers inline and attached provisional term sheet via DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/proposal/HL-2026-11-001

- Billing cadence: Net-30 monthly invoices by default. Quarterly prepay is available for an additional 3% discount; annual prepay available for a larger uplift. We can reflect your preference in the term sheet.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted data flow diagram are available; I've shared via the secure link in the SharePoint folder (see related_links). Primary contact for security evidence is security@redwood.ai — I'll introduce them if you want a direct call.
- Burst: burst capacity is best-effort with a contractual uplift and a capped number of guaranteed burst hours (we proposed 72 hours/month at 1.5x blended billing). For stronger guarantees we offer a higher-tier SLA (enterprise) with reserved burst lanes and explicit uptime credits — that's negotiable in the SOW.
- Cancellation & mid-term changes: mid-term reductions are allowed with 60-day notice; credits are pro-rated but break fees may apply depending on the reserved discount level. Exact language is in the term sheet.

If the team is aligned I can send an updated MAP with targeted dates for your requested kickoff window (week of Nov 30). Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk legal/procurement through the DocuSign.

— Laura
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
